item.title: JPMorgan Team Sees Credibility Risk in Treasury’s Bond Buybacks
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. strategists warned that markets may view the US Treasury’s surprise effort to curb long-term borrowing costs as lacking credibility, potentially pushing up the term premium and yields over time.

item.title: US-Canada Trade Draft Piles Pressure on Mexico to Match Terms
item.description: Canada’s preliminary trade deal with the US caught Mexican officials and business leaders off guard. Now, Mexico wants one of its own, as questions grow over whether months of painstaking engagement can deliver comparable tariff relief from President Donald Trump.

item.title: Investors See 10-Year Treasury Yields at 5% Hurting EM Asia Debt
item.description: Global funds see any rise in Treasury 10-year yields toward 5% spurring outflows from emerging Asian bonds, as higher rates in the US will prompt investors to favor dollar assets over regional debt.

item.title: Australia Regulator to Review Bank Lending as Credit Slows
item.description: Australia’s prudential regulator will monitor lending practices across the country’s banks in an effort to ensure slowing credit growth does not lead to riskier loans.

item.title: CK Hutchison Seeks $1.5 Billion for Loss of Panama Assets
item.description: CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd. commenced international arbitration proceedings against Panama, seeking more than $1.5 billion in damages over the loss of its investments in two ports on the country’s strategic canal.

item.title: Japan’s Exports Grow at Fastest Pace Since 2022 on Chips
item.description: Japan’s export growth accelerated to the fastest pace since 2022, fueled by robust demand for chips and cars and a yen that weakened to a 40-year low.

item.title: Australia ‘Outraged’ at Israel Ending Probe of Aid Worker Death
item.description: Australia’s government said it is “outraged” that Israel failed to charge any of the soldiers responsible for the 2024 killing of an Australian aid worker, with Canberra planning to formally protest the decision.

item.title: Asian School Chain Founder Seeks $300 Million for PE Buyout Fund
item.description: A newly launched private equity firm is seeking up to $300 million for its debut fund to acquire school assets across Asia and the Middle East, the latest attempt to capitalize on demand from rich families for quality education.

item.title: Gold Holds Near $4,500 as US Treasury Buyback Sends Yields Lower
item.description: Gold held the biggest gain in six months after the Treasury Department made a surprise move to rein in long-term borrowing costs.

item.title: Miner Fortescue’s Profit Falls as China Challenges Persist
item.description: Fortescue Ltd.’s full-year profit fell as the Australian iron ore miner struggled with delays to its major growth project, while difficult negotiations with China’s state-backed buyer continue to weigh on the outlook.

item.title: Apple’s Camera-Equipped AI AirPods Remain on Track for 2027 Despite Video Leak
item.description: An Apple Inc. effort to sell camera-equipped AirPods remains on track for 2027, despite a leak from the company indicating that the product might arrive sooner.

item.title: Japan’s 20-Year Bond Auction Faces Test as Global Yields Surge
item.description: Japan’s sale of 20-year government bonds on Thursday will test whether elevated yields are enough to lure buyers back to the long end as a global debt selloff piles pressure on the market.

item.title: BlackRock, Oaktree Seize Movie Servicer With $900 Million Debt
item.description: BlackRock Inc.’s HPS and Brookfield Corp.’s Oaktree Capital Management took over a firm that provides lighting, rigging and other services for Hollywood productions, wiping out as much as $900 million of debt as the global entertainment industry struggles with changing economics, according to people with knowledge of the deal.

item.title: Behind the Bond Market Rollercoaster and Bessent’s Treasury Intervention
item.description: On Monday, US Bonds Saw a Sell-Off. On Wednesday, Bessent Stepped In

item.title: Asian Stocks to Gain as US Treasury Supports Bonds: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to rebound, tracking Wall Street’s broad gains after US officials said they plan to boost buybacks of longer dated Treasuries to help ease borrowing costs following a surge in yields to near multi-decade highs.

item.title: AIA Posts Growth in New Business Value on Hong Kong, China
item.description: AIA Group Ltd. reported 13% growth in new business value in the first half of this year, led by strong sales in key markets including Hong Kong and China.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 19
item.description: Oil held a four-day run of gains as traders assessed the standoff in the Middle East between Iran and the US, with signs some crude is being shipped through the Strait of Hormuz to global markets.

item.title: Hong Kong Banks Turn to Student Housing as Property Bright Spot
item.description: The aging Regal Oriental Hotel is hardly a Hong Kong hotspot, yet in recent weeks it’s become a popular destination for bankers from some of the city’s top lenders, some of whom made repeat visits.

item.title: Bessent Becomes Most Interventionist Treasury Chief in Decades
item.description: With a slew of unexpected maneuvers this year, Scott Bessent has emerged as the most interventionist Treasury secretary in financial markets in decades — putting his credibility on the line in an effort to quell a potentially damaging rise in US borrowing costs.

item.title: Bets on Long-Bond ETF Spiked a Day Before US Announced Buyback
item.description: One or more investors piled into an exchange-traded fund that’s highly sensitive to swings in long-term US bond yields on Tuesday, a day before the Treasury Department unexpectedly ramped up buybacks of long-dated debt and sparked a rally.

item.title: US vs China AI Race: How ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Kimi Agents Compare
item.description: A spate of new releases show Chinese competitors are closing the gap on Silicon Valley, and winning market share with lower prices.

item.title: Trump Opens Door to Hyperliquid as US Pulls Crypto Trade Onshore
item.description: President Donald Trump said US regulators are working to bring Hyperliquid, a fast-growing crypto platform, into the country, offering one of the clearest signals yet that the White House wants to pull a major piece of the industry’s offshore market infrastructure onshore.

item.title: US Public Debt Hits $40 Trillion, Raising ‘Doom Loop’ Risk
item.description: Total US public debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time, and has now surged by a third in less than five years, as US lawmakers continue to shrug off calls to contend with historically wide fiscal deficits.

item.title: Why High Yields on Government Bonds Are Causing Alarm
item.description: Government borrowing costs have been surging around the world as investors demand more compensation to entice them to hold longer-maturity debt. Average bond yields across the Group of Seven countries hit their highest level since 2008 in mid-August.

item.title: CFTC Considers AI Compute Futures as ICE, CME Eye New Market
item.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is asking for public input on futures contracts for the computing power that undergirds the artificial intelligence sector as industry heavyweights move to embrace so-called compute as a tradable asset.

item.title: Guggenheim’s Beaten-Down Loan Whipsaws as Lenders Digest Call
item.description: A loan issued by the financing entity of Guggenheim Investments whipsawed on Wednesday after executives reiterated to lenders that earnings would likely improve in the third quarter while steering clear of details about the wide-ranging probe into Mark Walter’s business empire.

item.title: SpaceX Attempted to Acquire AI Coding Startup Cognition
item.description: SpaceX approached artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. about a potential acquisition, according to people familiar with the matter, in what would have been its second large takeover in recent months to gain ground in the AI race.

item.title: Operation Twist Redux: Bessent Moves Evoke Crisis-Fighting Fed
item.description: The Trump administration’s surprise move to ramp up buybacks of long-dated Treasuries is drawing parallels with the Federal Reserve’s “Operation Twist,” a strategy that was last deployed in 2011 to pull down bond yields.

item.title: AI Chip Startup Fractile in Talks for $6.5 Billion Value After Anthropic Deal
item.description: Fractile, a startup developing chips tailored for artificial intelligence use that has a deal to supply Anthropic PBC, is in advanced talks to notch a valuation more than six times higher than the price it landed in May.

item.title: TrueCar CEO Sees Auto-Industry Peril as Tariff Threat Sows Doubt
item.description: TrueCar Inc. Chief Executive Officer Scott Painter warned that US-Canada trade uncertainty poses a greater threat to the auto industry than tariffs themselves because it upends manufacturers’ decision-making ability.
